messages:
Noah Kim: Quick sync after the postmortem - we need final decisions on comms scope: statuspage language, who gets the full RCA, and whether to trigger customer emails for recurring flaps. I opened a lightweight tracker: https://ourdocs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-117/tracker :clipboard:

incident-bot: Postmortem uploaded: https://ourdocs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-117/postmortem (owner: @Noah Kim) :page_facing_up:

Sofia Alvarez: For statuspage wording proposal: use 'Service disruption' for user-visible errors OR latency > p95 threshold, and reserve 'Partial outage' only for when a majority of routing region is unreachable. Keeps public copy concise.

Ethan Brooks: +1. Suggest concrete thresholds for consistency: errors >=0.5% for >10m OR p95 >= 3s for >10m => 'Service disruption'. Otherwise say 'Degraded performance'.

Maya Singh: We keep seeing small inference-proxy flaps every ~3 days. Recommend a recurring incident tag in tracker so ops/devs get a weekly digest. I'll own the pattern analysis (A4) and run a weekly query.

Noah Kim: Thanks Maya. Can you add the query + sample cron to the tracker?

Maya Singh: Yep. Adding now. Cron snippet I use: ```# run weekly pattern job
0 6 * * 1 /usr/local/bin/incident-patterns --incident INC-2026-117 --window 30d --out /tmp/inc-117.json || echo "pattern job failed" | mail -s "pattern job failure" ops@redwood.com```

Ethan Brooks: On RCA sharing: proposal is two-tier: 1) publish a short redacted customer-facing summary within 48h (auto-post to statuspage + email to subscribed customers), 2) full technical RCA available to customers under NDA/on request within 10 business days. Security + Legal must approve redactions before publish.

Sofia Alvarez: I prefer 72h for the public summary to allow triage team to confirm mitigations. 48h is tight for complex outages. Maybe set 48h target for small incidents, 72h default for anything with cross-team impact.

Noah Kim: OK compromise: target 48h for incidents with single-owner fixes and limited blast radius; 72h for multi-team. We'll annotate incident severity in the tracker and the template will pick the right deadline.

Ethan Brooks: Who signs off redactions? Current policy: Security + Incident Owner + Legal for customer-facing docs. Can we allow Security to approve low-risk log redactions without Legal if the incident is internal-only?

Sofia Alvarez: I think redaction exceptions need an explicit whitelist. Let's add an "exceptions" tab in the tracker and require Security to log the reason. Legal stays in the loop for external comms unless Security flags low risk.

Noah Kim: Action owners: A1: statuspage copy - Sofia to finalize + link to tracker; A2: public summary SLA field in template - Noah to update template; A3: redaction approval flow - Ethan to propose flow + list, Legal to review; A4: recurring pattern analysis - Maya to run query & send weekly digest.

incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: A1 statuspage draft due 2026-05-02T10:00:00Z (owner: Sofia Alvarez).

Sofia Alvarez: I'll draft two variants: short statuspage-friendly blurb and a longer 72h customer summary with suggested CTAs for support teams.

Ethan Brooks: I'll draft the redaction checklist and a small approval webhook we can integrate with tracker so approvers can tick boxes. Simple example payload below:
```json
{"incident":"INC-2026-117","action":"redaction_approval","approver":"security@redwood.com","approved":true}
```

Noah Kim: Great. Let's keep comms simple and consistent. I'll push the template changes tonight and loop in Legal for quick review on the redaction checklist. Follow-up sync in 36h to confirm statuspage copy and RCA timing. :calendar:
